annotation.method: Codex freshly read the complete 37-page paper in physical-PDF order, including all appendices, surveyed every named proved result, compared candidates with the frozen Mathlib and importable NumStability baselines, and privately formalized the selected convergence argument before packaging it.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 3, the stationary fast-matrix-multiplication error bound
rejected_candidates.reason: The importable library has only generic dot-product and conventional matrix-product bounds. It has no recursive bilinear-algorithm theorem, so the source result does not obtain the exactly-one-result T1 speedup; treating several wrappers around the same dot-product analysis as independent would also not satisfy T2.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 5, the uniform nonstationary fast-matrix-multiplication error bound
rejected_candidates.reason: This extension depends on the same unavailable recursive fast-multiplication machinery as Theorem 3 rather than at least two independent substantial importable results.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Propositions 9, 11, and 12, the outside, inside, and repeated scaling error bounds
rejected_candidates.reason: Once the paper's abstract O(epsilon) fast-product premise is supplied, these proofs are mainly paper-specific scaling identities and max-norm inequalities. The available conventional matrix-product theorem neither states the premise for a fast algorithm nor creates the required tier speedup.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 18, monotonicity of the repeated-scaling envelope
rejected_candidates.reason: It is source-faithful and has no corresponding library result, but its two one-step max-norm arguments are materially easier than the selected infinite-tail linear-convergence proof and do not safely meet the T3 difficulty floor.
Its proof is a shorter consequence of Lemma 21's estimates plus logarithm and exponential algebra. Lemma 21 is the stronger, more fundamental, and more difficult source-supported T3 target.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 22, asymptotic sharpness of the one-half rate
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly omits the calculation of the alternating scaling iterates. Selecting it would either rely on missing source proof material or reduce to a much easier closed-form scalar limit after assuming those iterates.

rejected_candidates.candidate: algorithm searches and numerical experiments in Sections 5-7
rejected_candidates.reason: These are search procedures, measured comparisons, and empirical observations rather than additional universally proved conclusions.

T1.decision: Skipped. No source-faithful theorem needs exactly one substantial importable NumStability result that makes L substantially faster than N.

T2.decision: Skipped. No source candidate needs at least two independent substantial importable NumStability results; conventional matrix multiplication is only a short wrapper around the same dot-product analysis, and the directly relevant fast-recursion modules are not in the frozen compiled set.

T3.decision: Use the cycle-reindexed analytic core of Lemma 21: construct and validate the exponential infinite-tail majorant that completes Theorem 13's linear-convergence proof.

selection_policy: Use only conclusions explicitly stated and proved in the paper.
Reindex the paper's paired times t=t0+2n by complete outside-inside cycles without changing the mathematical content.
Do not count several wrappers around one dot-product analysis as independent substantial library results.
Do not formalize Lemma 22 because its scaling-iterate calculation is omitted in the source.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source, its importable compiled subset, and Mathlib.
